subject: Root's planned chonkstep-darwin/darwin-ipc/ port of chonk-ipc after desktop-shell-build-001/check.log (11 E0425 errors, all in crates/chonk-ipc/src/lib.rs: SOCK_CLOEXEC/SOCK_NONBLOCK at L113/L136/L206, accept4 at L206, ucred/SO_PEERCRED at L223-227). Live snapshots stay untouched.

source_facts.no_atomic_flags: Pinned XNU bsd/sys/socket.h defines no SOCK_CLOEXEC, SOCK_NONBLOCK or accept4. On Darwin, close-on-exec and non-blocking must be set by a separate fcntl after socket() or accept().
source_facts.accept_inheritance: XNU accept copies the listener's file flags (fflag = fp->f_flag; fp->f_flag = fflag) and sets SS_NBIO from FNONBLOCK, so an accepted fd inherits O_NONBLOCK from a non-blocking listener. Close-on-exec is a per-descriptor flag and is not inherited; every accepted fd starts inheritable.
source_facts.sockaddr_un: sys/un.h: {u8 sun_len; sa_family_t sun_family; char sun_path[104]}. getsockaddr bounds addrlen to [2, SOCK_MAXADDRLEN=255] and overwrites sa_len with it; unp_bind uses namelen = sun_len - offsetof(sun_path) and treats sun_path as not NUL-terminated. chonk's existing #[cfg(target_os="macos")] branch already sets sun_len and returns addrlen = offsetof(sun_path) + len + 1, with paths limited to fewer than 104 bytes.
source_facts.peer_credentials: uipc_ctloutput (uipc_usrreq.c:828-875): LOCAL_PEERCRED returns the unp_peercred struct xucred only when UNP_HAVEPC is set (otherwise ENOTCONN for stream, EINVAL otherwise). On a stream connect the accepted socket stores the connecting thread's credentials (:1429-1436), and the client gets the listener's cached credentials (:1466-1468, :2773-2775), so it is a connect-time snapshot. libc getpeereid (libSystem/libc/gen/FreeBSD/getpeereid.c) calls getsockopt(fd, 0, LOCAL_PEERCRED), rejects cr_version != XUCRED_VERSION with EINVAL, and returns cr_uid/cr_gid. LOCAL_PEERPID returns peerso->last_pid, which so_update_last_owner_locked rewrites on bind, listen, accept, connect, send, receive, sopoll and kqfilter (uipc_socket.c:400-423, 11 call sites); kernel-created sockets keep last_pid 0. It is the last process to touch the peer socket at query time, not a connect-time PID like Linux SO_PEERCRED.
source_facts.spawn: XNU supports POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT (spawn.h 0x4000; kern_exec.c:3764+), which closes every fd not named in file actions at exec, atomically. chonk-shell is multithreaded and spawns from background threads (button_layout.rs:93 inside the thread at :133; appearance gsettings at appearance.rs:261). Its spawn wrappers use std::process::Command with null stdio and no pre_exec (spawn.rs:98-104, :213). Whether the pinned Rust std uses posix_spawn with POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT on Apple could not be verified: no rust-src for the toolchain is present.
source_facts.current_use_of_pid: No authorization in this source uses the IPC peer pid. Authorization uses the uid via peer_is_this_user (control.rs:902, hyprland-ipc server.rs:1004) and peer_is_this_user_or_root (server.rs:1018), both failing closed (unwrap_or(false)). window.pid in hyprland-ipc is a Wayland-client pid from a different source; its Darwin origin is outside this IPC port and should be checked separately.

contract_for_darwin_branch: C1 Creation (connect and bind): socket(AF_UNIX, kind, 0), then fcntl(F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) and an F_GETFL/F_SETFL read-modify-write adding O_NONBLOCK, each checked. On any failure close the fd and return the error, so a partially configured fd never escapes.

C2 Accept: accept(listener, NULL, NULL); EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN/EINTR give Ok(None), as on Linux. Then fcntl(F_SETFD, FD_CLOEXEC) and an explicit O_NONBLOCK set on the new fd (do not rely on the inherited FNONBLOCK), each checked, closing the new fd on failure.

C3 Credentials: uid/gid only from getpeereid; pid only from getsockopt(SOL_LOCAL=0, LOCAL_PEERPID, &pid, &len) requiring rc 0, len == sizeof(pid_t) and pid > 0. Any failure is an error. Never substitute getuid/geteuid/getpid/0 for the peer. Comparing the peer uid with the process's own geteuid() stays as on Linux.

C4 Semantics: document PeerCredentials.pid on Darwin as 'last-owner pid at query time'. It must not be used for authorization or connect-time identity. uid authorization keeps exactly both existing policies (same-uid; same-uid-or-root only for the command socket), with no widening.
C5 Address: keep the existing macOS sockaddr_un branch (sun_len plus exact addrlen, < 104 bytes, no NUL bytes).
C6 Linux: the non-macOS path keeps SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK, accept4 and SO_PEERCRED byte-identical, behind cfg, with its existing tests.
cloexec_implications: Between socket()/accept() and fcntl(FD_CLOEXEC), a spawn on another chonk-shell thread inherits the fd, unless that spawn closes non-inherited fds itself. Concrete effects: a leaked listening socket keeps the display socket 'live' after the shell exits, so clear_stale_socket refuses the next session as an existing owner; queued client connects also stall. A leaked accepted fd keeps a client connection half-open after the server closes it (no EOF to the client), and any I/O or poll by the holder would change the LOCAL_PEERPID answer. On Linux none of this happens, because the flags are atomic.
must_block_desktop_integration: B1: any credential fallback (fake or own uid/pid, zero) or any use of LOCAL_PEERPID for authorization or identity.

B2: an unproven fd-leak window. Before integration, show one of: (a) the pinned toolchain's std, by its source or by disassembly of the built chonk-shell, spawns through posix_spawn with POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT for every Command path used; or (b) all process spawns in chonk-shell are serialized against IPC fd creation and accept by a single audited lock; or (c) a Darwin spawn wrapper that sets POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT explicitly (with stdio file actions) replaces every spawn site.
B3: a partially configured fd (fcntl failure) returned to callers, or Ok returned after a failed fcntl.
B4: any change to Linux behavior or tests.
non_blocking: sun_len and addrlen handling (already correct in the macOS branch)
the 104-byte path limit with the current runtime directory
accepted O_NONBLOCK inheritance, given C2's explicit set
unknowns: Rust std's Apple posix_spawn flags in the pinned toolchain
the origin of window.pid in the Darwin compositor path
not_claimed: code correctness of the port (not written yet)
scope: Read-only: check.log, chonk-ipc/chonk-shell sources in desktop-shell-build-001, pinned XNU (uipc_usrreq.c, uipc_socket.c, uipc_syscalls.c, sys/un.h, sys/socket.h, sys/spawn.h, kern_exec.c), pinned libc getpeereid.c, canonical libSystem exports. No code, builds or hardware.
